value.rationale: At the natural finite Morse–Hedlund threshold the result solves the whole labeled-word population problem for every \(q,k,L\) with \(L\ge 2k\). A unique boundary-normal primitive core establishes genuine disjoint counting, giving an exact Möbius formula, immediate constancy beyond length \(2k\), and nontrivial asymptotics \(q^k\) times a quadratic factor. This is a global structural enumeration with potential utility in low-complexity word analysis and test-instance generation, not an arbitrary finite slice.
